params.body:
## Why

`php artisan down --with-secret` showed a page written for engineers: a huge blue "503", a dark card, "Even in onderhoud", "Probeer het over een paar minuten opnieuw" and a button "Terug naar het dashboard" that lands on the same 503. The person who sees it is a garage employee on a phone between two customers. The number means "broken" to them, the button is a dead control, and a promise of minutes that turns into hours is worse than no promise.

## What changed

`resources/views/errors/503.blade.php` is now a standalone page (no longer extends `errors.layout`; the 403, 404, 419, 429 and 500 pages keep the shared layout untouched):

- Heading: **Stocklist Dealer verhuist vandaag naar een nieuwe server**
- Body: *Je gegevens zijn veilig; je hoeft niets te doen. Zodra de verhuis klaar is, verschijnt Stocklist Dealer hier weer vanzelf.*
- *Vragen? Neem contact op.* linking to `https://stocklistdealer.eu/#contact`, the same Contact link the guest layout footer shows. No button to the dashboard.
- A quiet mono line "deze pagina vernieuwt zichzelf" with a 5px progress groove that fills over the refresh interval (colour only in the moving part; still under `prefers-reduced-motion`).
- Footer, small mono: "verhuis" and "503", so the code stays findable without being the headline.
- Paper ground by default; dark palette only via `prefers-color-scheme: dark`, which the shared error layout already supported.
- No Vite, no app layout: all styling inline, the logo component already carries its own styles. Renders during maintenance in every configuration, and also through `down --render=errors::503` (prerendered before Composer loads).

## How the refresh interval is sourced

`<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="{{ $retry }}">` where `$retry` is, in order: the `Refresh` header if `down --refresh=` was given, else the `Retry-After` header from `$exception->getHeaders()` (Laravel 12's `PreventRequestsDuringMaintenance` sets it from `--retry=`, and `Handler::renderHttpException` passes the exception to the view), else `$retryAfter` (what `down --render` passes), else 60 seconds. So `php artisan down --with-secret --retry=60` gives a page that reloads every 60 seconds and comes back by itself when the site is up.

## Changing the text on the day

The text lives in the view. There is no `--message` option in Laravel 12's `down` command and no env or config hook in this PR, so changing the wording means a merge and a deploy (Forge deploys fine while the site is down; the deploy does not lift maintenance mode). I chose not to add a `MAINTENANCE_MESSAGE` env value: with `config:cache` an `env()` call in a view returns null, and a config key would have touched `config/app.php`, outside the scope of this change.

## Rule and test

- `docs/bedrijfsregels/33-p3-integraties.md`, R P3-12.1: extended with what the visitor sees (plain heading, no duration, self-refresh on Retry-After, no dashboard button, contact link).
- `tests/Feature/MaintenanceModeTest.php`: two new tests tagged `@rule P3-12.1`: the ordinary page answers 503 with the heading, the meta refresh (`content="60"`), the self-refresh line, no `href="/"`, no "Terug naar het dashboard", no `err-code`, no "minuten"; and with `retry => 120` the header and the meta refresh both say 120.

`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='Maintenance|Error|RulesCoverage|RulesIdentity'`: OK (21 tests, 68 assertions); with StylesheetSyntax added, OK (24 tests, 709 assertions).
params.title: A maintenance page for people, not a 503 for engineers
